:::{#exm-taylor-1d}
#### The remainder point for $e^x$

Take $g(x) = e^x$ on $[0, 1]$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
g' &= g'' \\
&= g.
\end{aligned}
$$

@thm-taylor-1d says $e = 1 + 1 + \tfrac{1}{2}\,e^{\midpt}$ for some $\midpt \in (0, 1)$.
Solving,

$$
\begin{aligned}
e^{\midpt} &= 2 (e - 2) \\
&\approx 2 \times 0.71828 \\
&= 1.43656,
\end{aligned}
$$

so $\midpt = \log 1.43656 \approx 0.362$,
where $\log$ is the [natural logarithm](algebra.qmd#def-natural-log).
This $\midpt$ is in $(0, 1)$.

:::
